text: Pataxó Hã-Ha-Hãe is a dormant language of Brazil. It belongs to the Maxakalian language family. The language is no longer used as a first language by any remaining members of the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

text: Los Pataxó Hã-Hã-Hãe son un pueblo indígena del sur del estado de Bahía, distinto de los Pataxó del litoral (Porto Seguro). Su núcleo territorial es la Tierra Indígena Caramuru-Paraguaçu, situada entre los municipios de Itaju do Colônia, Pau Brasil, Camamu e Itabuna, en el sur baiano cacaotero.

title: Pataxó
text: Land disputes involving the Pataxó, particularly the Pataxó Hã-Hã-Hãe subgroup in southern Bahia state, center on efforts to reclaim territories demarcated as indigenous but occupied by farmers, ranchers, and eucalyptus plantations since the mid-20th century.

text: Pataxó (Patashó), or Pataxó Hã-Ha-Hãe (Pataxó-Hãhaãi), is an extinct Maxakalían language of Brazil formerly spoken by the Pataxó people of the Bahia region, and of Minas Gerais, Pôsto Paraguassu in Itabuna municipality.
